title: 2011 · 英语一 · Text 1
description: 22 个标黄/选项词 + 5 个高价值短语。轻复习优先题目关键与错题词，不要求一次背完。

book.definition: vt. 宣布，通知；郑重地说；通报

cards.quote: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009.
cards.meaning: 宣布；公告；此处指任命消息的公布
cards.translation: 纽约爱乐乐团决定聘请艾伦·吉尔伯特担任下一任音乐总监；自2009年突然公布这一任命以来，这个决定就一直是古典音乐界热议的话题。
cards.note: 词表收录的是动词 announce；announcement 是其名词形式。
cards.match: 派生词语境；关联词条 announce
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页

book.definition: adj. 谦虚谨慎的，不爱炫耀的

cards.quote: Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert’s appointment in the Times, calls him “an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him.”
cards.translation: 就连曾在《纽约时报》倡议任命吉尔伯特的托马西尼，也称他为“一位谦逊朴实、毫无令人敬畏的大指挥家派头的音乐家”。
cards.note: 第22题里它可对应 modest，重点是“不摆架子、不炫耀”。
cards.match: 词条对应
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页
cards.collocationMeaning: 一位谦逊朴实的音乐家

book.definition: adj. 令人敬畏的，难对付的

cards.quote: Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert’s appointment in the Times, calls him “an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him.”
cards.translation: 就连曾在《纽约时报》倡议任命吉尔伯特的托马西尼，也称他为“一位谦逊朴实、毫无令人敬畏的大指挥家派头的音乐家”。
cards.note: 这里不是“可怕”这么简单，而是带有强势、令人敬畏的气场。
cards.match: 词条对应
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页

book.definition: n. 描述，叙述；种类，类型

cards.quote: As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.
cards.translation: 对于一支此前一直由古斯塔夫·马勒、皮埃尔·布列兹这类音乐家执掌的乐团来说，用这种话描述它的下一任音乐总监，至少在部分《纽约时报》读者看来，恐怕只是勉强的称赞。
cards.note: 注意 As a description of：作为对……的描述。
cards.match: 词条对应
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页
cards.collocation: a description of the next music director
cards.collocationMeaning: 对下一任音乐总监的描述

book.definition: n. 管弦乐队；(剧场) 正厅前排座位

cards.quote: As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.
cards.translation: 对于一支此前一直由古斯塔夫·马勒、皮埃尔·布列兹这类音乐家执掌的乐团来说，用这种话描述它的下一任音乐总监，至少在部分《纽约时报》读者看来，恐怕只是勉强的称赞。
cards.note: 本文中的 Philharmonic 指纽约爱乐乐团；orchestra 是管弦乐队。
cards.match: 词条对应
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页

book.definition: adv. 迄今，到 (某时) 为止

cards.quote: As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.
cards.translation: 对于一支此前一直由古斯塔夫·马勒、皮埃尔·布列兹这类音乐家执掌的乐团来说，用这种话描述它的下一任音乐总监，至少在部分《纽约时报》读者看来，恐怕只是勉强的称赞。

book.definition: adj. 管弦乐的，管弦乐队的

cards.quote: To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting orchestral music.
cards.translation: 诚然，他演奏的有趣作品种类丰富，令人印象深刻；但为了听到有趣的管弦乐，我没有必要前往艾弗里·费舍尔音乐厅或其他任何地方。
cards.note: orchestra 是名词，orchestral 是形容词。
cards.match: 词条对应
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页

book.definition: n. 代替者，代替物；替补运动员；vi. vt. 替换，取代

cards.quote: Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point.
cards.translation: 那些回应说“录音无法替代现场演出”的忠实音乐会观众，没有抓住问题的关键。
cards.note: substitute 作名词时是“替代物”；本句最好连 no substitute for 一起记。
cards.match: 词条对应
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页

book.definition: n. 仪器；乐器；仪表；手段；工具

cards.quote: For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century.
cards.translation: 为了争夺艺术爱好者的时间、注意力和金钱，古典器乐演奏者不仅必须与歌剧院、舞团、剧团和博物馆竞争，还必须与20世纪古典音乐大师的演奏录音竞争。
cards.note: 词表未单列 instrumentalist；可由 instrument（乐器）理解为“器乐演奏者”。
cards.match: 派生词语境；关联词条 instrument
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页

book.definition: n. 巡回剧团，戏班子，歌舞团

cards.quote: For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century.
cards.meaning: 剧团，歌舞团；此处指舞团
cards.translation: 为了争夺艺术爱好者的时间、注意力和金钱，古典器乐演奏者不仅必须与歌剧院、舞团、剧团和博物馆竞争，还必须与20世纪古典音乐大师的演奏录音竞争。
cards.note: dance troupe＝舞团；注意 troupe 与 troop（军队、群体）区分。

book.definition: n. 博物馆

cards.quote: For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century.
cards.translation: 为了争夺艺术爱好者的时间、注意力和金钱，古典器乐演奏者不仅必须与歌剧院、舞团、剧团和博物馆竞争，还必须与20世纪古典音乐大师的演奏录音竞争。

book.definition: vi. vt. (使) 振动，(使) 颤动

cards.quote: Gilbert’s own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into “a markedly different, more vibrant organization.”
cards.meaning: 充满活力的；生机勃勃的
cards.translation: 吉尔伯特本人对新音乐的兴趣已广受关注：古典音乐评论家亚历克斯·罗斯称，他有能力把爱乐乐团变成“一个明显不同、更加充满活力的组织”。
cards.note: 词表收录相关词 vibrate（振动）；vibrant 在这里取“充满活力的”。
cards.match: 派生词语境；关联词条 vibrate
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页
cards.collocation: a markedly different, more vibrant organization
cards.collocationMeaning: 一个明显不同、更有活力的组织

book.definition: n. 全部节目，曲目；全部技能

cards.quote: Merely expanding the orchestra’s repertoire will not be enough.
cards.translation: 仅仅扩大乐团的曲目范围还不够。
cards.note: 音乐语境里优先记“曲目、保留剧目”。
cards.match: 词条对应

book.definition: n. 约定，预约；任命，指派；职位

cards.quote: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009.
cards.meaning: 任命，指派；此处指任命 Gilbert
cards.translation: 纽约爱乐乐团决定聘请艾伦·吉尔伯特担任下一任音乐总监；自2009年突然公布这一任命以来，这个决定就一直是古典音乐界热议的话题。
cards.note: 本篇 appointment 不是“预约”，而是“任命”。
cards.match: 词条对应
cards.readingSource: 2011年考研英语一 · Text 1 · 试卷第3—4页

book.definition: vt. 招致，引起，蒙受

cards.quote: The decision incurred criticism from several musicians.
cards.translation: 这个决定招致了几位音乐家的批评。
cards.note: incur criticism＝招致批评。原文中任命的总体反响是积极的，不要把原题干扰项记成文章事实。
cards.match: 原文变形 → 词表原形

book.definition: n. 怀疑，嫌疑，猜疑；猜想，预感

cards.quote: The sudden change raised suspicion among the staff.
cards.translation: 这一突然的变化引起了员工的怀疑。
cards.note: raise suspicion＝引起怀疑。此例另写；它不表示文中吉尔伯特的任命确实引起了怀疑。
cards.match: 词条对应

book.definition: n. 好奇心；奇物，珍品

cards.quote: The unusual concert title aroused my curiosity.
cards.translation: 这个不同寻常的音乐会标题引起了我的好奇心。
cards.note: arouse curiosity＝引起好奇心。补充例句只帮助记忆搭配，不替代原题证据。
cards.match: 词条对应

cards.quote: Travel expenses made the concert more costly for visitors.
cards.translation: 交通费用使观众参加这场音乐会的总花费更高。

cards.quote: The advertisement exaggerated the variety of the performances.
cards.translation: 这则广告夸大了演出的多样性。
cards.note: exaggerate＝夸大。原题C项不是正确结论；补充例句只展示词义和搭配。

cards.quote: We should not overestimate the value of a famous name.
cards.translation: 我们不应高估名气的价值。

book.definition: n. 部分；成员；零件；区域；角色；vi. 离开，分别；vt. 分离，分开；adv. 在一定程度上，部分地

cards.quote: For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least.
cards.translation: 总体而言，反响是积极的——这么说已经很保守了。
cards.note: for the most part≈generally/mostly，表示总体而言；原句是第21题的定位依据。

book.definition: adj. (光、声等) 微弱的；渺茫的；vi. 晕倒，昏厥；n. 昏厥
n. 称赞，赞美；(对上帝的) 称颂；vt. 称赞，赞美；称颂，感谢 (上帝)

cards.quote: As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.
cards.meaning: 勉强的赞扬，不痛不痒的称赞
cards.translation: 对于一支此前一直由古斯塔夫·马勒、皮埃尔·布列兹这类音乐家执掌的乐团来说，用这种话描述它的下一任音乐总监，至少在部分《纽约时报》读者看来，恐怕只是勉强的称赞。
cards.note: faint 在这里不是“晕倒”，而是“微弱的”；faint praise 常带“夸得不够、甚至像没夸”的意味。

cards.quote: Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point.
